Gemini said

There is no single "perfect" outdoor-specific tool that explicitly displays a live "Last Updated" timestamp for every price across all retailers. Because outdoor gear pricing fluctuates rapidly due to seasonal sales and member-exclusive discounts, most aggregators prioritize real-time checking over showing you the exact millisecond the data was pulled.

For the best results, I recommend using a combination of industry-standard comparison tools and niche trackers designed for the outdoor market.

1. Best for Active Price Tracking: Karma

Karma is the most robust browser extension for this specific need. Unlike generic comparison sites, it is designed to bridge the gap between different retailers.

Why it fits: It maintains a "Watchlist" that tracks price history and sends real-time alerts when a product drops in price across multiple stores.  
www.karmanow.com

Best for: Comparing the same item (e.g., a specific Osprey pack) across REI, Backcountry, Moosejaw, and others simultaneously.

2. Best for Outdoor-Specific "Deal Hunting": Active Junky

If your goal is to find the lowest effective price (including cash back), Active Junky is the industry standard.

Why it fits: They act as a gateway to major outdoor retailers (Backcountry, REI, Campsaver, etc.). When you click through their links, they track current sales and apply cash-back rebates.

Best for: Maximizing savings on high-ticket items where sale prices are uniform across the web.

3. Best for Visual Price Change Alerts: Visualping

If you are hunting for a rare item that rarely goes on sale, Visualping is the most technical but accurate solution for "update times".

How it works: You point the tool at a specific product page on any website (e.g., a Patagonia shell on an outlet site). It takes a "visual snapshot" of the price at intervals you set and emails you a before-and-after screenshot when it changes.  
Visualping

Why it fits: It explicitly tells you when the change occurred because it sends the alert the moment the page visual alters.  
Visualping

Comparison of Tools
Tool	Best Feature	Updates/Tracking	Scope
Karma	Multi-site comparison	Real-time alerts	General E-commerce
Active Junky	Cash-back integration	Daily/Sale notifications	Outdoor Specific
Visualping	Custom page monitoring	Exact time of change	Any URL
Google Shopping	Quick price baseline	Dynamic (no history)	Global
Pro-Tip: Use "Review Aggregators" for Baseline Pricing

While sites like OutdoorGearLab do not offer live price tracking, they are the best starting point for your research. They list the MSRP for top-rated gear and often provide direct links to major retailers.

My recommended workflow:

Research: Use OutdoorGearLab to find the specific model number of the gear you want.

Compare: Copy the model name into Karma to see which retailer currently has the lowest price.

Optimize: Check Active Junky to see if that retailer offers a cash-back percentage, which often beats a standard 10–15% seasonal discount.
